23. Lastly, the learned Counsel for the appellant, submits that the place from where the accused-appellant brought out the arms and ammunition in question was an open place accessible to everyone and there is every likelihood of plantation in the absence of positive evidence that the accused appellant himself kept the alleged arms and ammunition under a heap of plastic. From the evidence on record we have found that the place from where the incriminating arms and ammunition were recovered i.e. western gate of BR Hall, is an open place which is accessible to others. It is also found from the evidence on record that the place of recovery was an abandoned place. So, admittedly, the arms and ammunition which were recovered as per showing and bringing out by the appellant was a place which is an open place where anyone can enter. That being the position as regard the place of recovery which is found from the evidence on record, the natural presumption would be that in the absence of any evidence to the contrary that the accused-appellant himself kept the alleged arms and ammunition, the whole case is a case of plantation. We do not find any evidence on record to show that the accused appellant Faruq himself kept the alleged arms and ammunition under the pile of plastic. In this respect the law governing the issue is very much settled and consistent. In several decisions of this Subcontinent it has been spelt out by the apex Court that when any arms and ammunition are recovered from an open place or a place accessible to everyone even if as per showing or pointing out by the accused, it is dangerous to convict such person solely on that score without any positive evidence to the contrary that he or they, himself or themselves, as the case may be, kept those arms and ammunition in that place. 

 24. Regard may be taken on this proposition of law to the decisions reported in Bhuboni Shaha vs The King 2 DLR (PC) 39, Arshadullah vs State 21 DLR 694, Daud Ali Daud Hossain vs State 27 DLR 251, Abul Hossain Master vs State 44 DLR 159,47 DLR 451, 49 DLR 16, 50 DLR 356, 551 and 515 and so many other decisions. So, in the instant case there is no denying as it is found from the evidence on record that the place of occurrence from where the arms and ammunition were recovered as per pointing and bringing out by the accused appellant was absolutely an open place accessible to others and, as such, in the absence of any evidence that the accused appellant himself kept the arms and ammunition in the place of recovery the natural presumption would be that appellant had no exclusive possession and control of the arms and ammunition in question conscientiously with mensrea. In that view of the matter, it is unsafe to hold that the accused appellant Md Faruk has committed an offence under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act in the manner as it has been stated by the prosecution in the first information report. It would be unjust and illegal to pass a conviction in such a situation, where from the entire evidence on record it is clearly found that the place of recovery of arms and ammunition even though shown by the appellant was an open place free for everyone to enter.
